title: Synergistic engineering of a zwitterion polymer-grafted COF–biochar hybrid composite membrane for flexible removal of cationic and/or anionic pollutants in complex aquatic environments: characterization, removal evaluation, kinetics, thermodynamics and mechanisms
content: The development of high-performance, stable, and reusable multimodality adsorbents is essential for remediating mixed inorganic contaminants in complex water matrices. To address this, a novel zwitterionic polymer graft covalent organic framework-biochar hybrid composite, designated as ZP-COF@BC, was successfully fabricated via in situ Schiff base solvothermal polymerization and surface-initiated radical grafting. This strategic integration combines the robust porosity and structural strength of biochar, the crystalline network of the COF, and the equal positively and negatively charged functional groups introduced by zwitterionic polymer chains, which significantly enhance electrostatic interactions and hydration layer formation. The resulting hybrid exhibits a uniform mesoporous structure with a specific surface area of 412.6 m2 g−1 and thermal stability up to 415 °C. Evaluation of its adsorption capabilities reveals exceptional broad-spectrum removal efficiencies for diverse inorganic pollutants, achieving maximum adsorption capacities of 93.2 mg g−1 for phosphate, 71.35 mg g−1 for arsenate, 119.25 mg g−1 for lead, and 100.65 mg g−1 for chromium(vi). Adsorption kinetics conform to the pseudo-second-order model, while equilibrium data best fit the Langmuir isotherm, indicating monolayer chemisorption. Furthermore, the composite demonstrates outstanding structural durability and reusability, retaining 91% of its removal efficiency across five consecutive regeneration cycles. Ultimately, the synergistic coupling of biochar porosity, COF crystallinity, and zwitterionic functionality provides an efficient and robust material platform for the simultaneous elimination of competing inorganic pollutants from complex aqueous environments.
